questions.question: Which festival of Kerala has entered the Guinness World Records for being the single largest gathering of women for a religious activity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Attukal Pongala**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__
 __ 
• **Attukal Pongala** is a famous festival celebrated in the state of **Kerala**, India. It is organized annually at the **Attukal Bhagavathy Temple** in Thiruvananthapuram. 
• The festival is renowned for its unique feature of being the **largest single gathering of women** in the world for a religious activity. This achievement has been recognized by the **Guinness World Records**. 
• The event involves thousands of women preparing a special offering called **Pongala**, made of rice, jaggery, and coconut, which is cooked in earthen pots as an offering to the goddess Attukal Devi. 
• The festival spans over ten days, with the **Pongala ritual** being the most significant and occurring on the ninth day. Women gather in and around the temple premises and on the streets of Thiruvananthapuram to participate in this ritual. 
• The festival is a symbolic representation of **devotion, equality, and empowerment of women**, as it unites women from all walks of life and religious backgrounds. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Significance of Attukal Pongala:** 
• The festival is dedicated to **Attukal Bhagavathy**, an incarnation of the Hindu goddess **Kannaki (Parvati).** 
• It is celebrated in the **Malayalam month of Kumbham** (February–March). 
• The festival represents the victory of good over evil and celebrates the **goddess’s power** to protect her devotees. 
• **Guinness World Records Recognition:** 
• The **2016 edition** of Attukal Pongala saw participation from more than **2.5 million women**, earning it the Guinness World Record for the **largest gathering of women** for a religious activity. 
• The record highlights the global cultural significance of the festival and its ability to bring women together in solidarity. 
• **Preparation for the Ritual:** 
• Women bring their own cooking utensils, ingredients, and firewood to prepare the Pongala offering on temporary hearths set up on roadsides and open spaces. 
• The ritual begins after the chief priest of the temple lights the **holy hearth (Pandara Aduppu)** inside the temple premises. 
• **Comparison with Other Kerala Festivals:** 
• **Chikalkalo:** A traditional mud festival celebrated in certain parts of Kerala, particularly in the Kasaragod district. It involves physical games and is not religious in nature. 
• **Pooram:** A temple festival celebrated with grand processions and fireworks. The most famous is the Thrissur Pooram. 
• **Vishu:** The Malayalam New Year celebrated in April, marked by feasting and the Vishukkani ritual. 
• **Attukal Pongala:** Stands out as a festival exclusively for women and holds spiritual and cultural importance. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Historical Background:** The temple is believed to be over **500 years old** and holds a significant place in Kerala's religious and cultural history. 
• **Equality and Inclusiveness:** Women from all castes, religions, and social backgrounds participate in the festival, making it a symbol of **unity and empowerment.** 
• **Economic Impact:** The festival contributes significantly to the local economy, as vendors sell cooking materials, food items, and earthen pots during the event.

questions.question:
**Consider the following statements regarding recent India-Maldives bilateral developments:****1. India announced a financial assistance package of USD 1.4 billion to Maldives during President Solih's 2018 visit.
2. The 6th Joint Commission Meeting (JCM) in 2019 included signing MoUs between the Financial Intelligence Units (FIUs) of both countries.
3. In 2020, India and Maldives signed an agreement for mutual support in climate risk insurance for island territories.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?**
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1 and 3**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• During the state visit of Maldives President **Ibrahim Mohamed Solih** to India in **December 2018**, the Indian government announced a major financial assistance package of **USD 1.4 billion**. This package was designed to support the Maldives in overcoming its debt crisis and included components like **Budgetary Support**, **Currency Swap** agreements, and **Concessional Lines of Credit**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The **6th Joint Commission Meeting (JCM)** between India and the Maldives was held in **New Delhi** on **December 13, 2019**. While the meeting focused on broad bilateral cooperation, the specific MoU between the **Financial Intelligence Units (FIUs)** of both countries to combat **Money Laundering** and **Terrorism Financing** was actually signed earlier in **June 2019** during Prime Minister Narendra Modi's visit to **Malé**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• In **2020**, the bilateral relationship expanded into environmental resilience, with both nations signing an agreement for cooperation in **Climate Change** and **Disaster Management**. This agreement specifically aimed at providing mutual support for **Climate Risk Insurance** and mitigation strategies tailored for the vulnerable **Island Territories** of the Maldives. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***

 **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Neighborhood First Policy** of India identifies the Maldives as a key partner in the **SAGAR** (Security and Growth for All in the Region) initiative.
 
 
• **Greater Malé Connectivity Project (GMCP):** In **2020**, India pledged a **USD 500 million** package (USD 100 million grant and USD 400 million Line of Credit) for the largest infrastructure project in the Maldives, connecting **Malé** with three neighboring islands.
 
• **Operation Sanjeevani:** During the **COVID-19 pandemic** in **2020**, India supplied **6.2 tonnes** of essential medicines to the Maldives, demonstrating proactive maritime cooperation.
 
• **Ekuverin:** This is the annual joint **Military Exercise** conducted between the Indian Army and the Maldives National Defence Force to enhance **Interoperability**.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements:

1. The Aditya-L1 mission was launched to replace the INSAT series of weather satellites.

2. Aditya-L1 successfully entered a Halo orbit around the Lagrange Point 1 (L1) to observe solar activity.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2 only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Aditya-L1** is India's first solar mission, designed to study the Sun's corona, solar emissions, and its impact on space weather.
 
• The mission successfully entered a **Halo orbit around the Lagrange Point 1 (L1)**, which is approximately 1.5 million km from Earth.
 
• The spacecraft will continuously observe the Sun without any interruptions caused by eclipses, leveraging the unique positioning at L1.
 
• Statement 1 is incorrect because **Aditya-L1 is not meant to replace INSAT weather satellites**; INSAT satellites primarily focus on Earth-based weather monitoring.
 
• Statement 2 is correct as Aditya-L1 achieved its intended orbit at L1 to conduct detailed studies on solar activities and their impact on the Earth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lagrange Point 1 (L1):** A position in space where the gravitational forces of the Earth and the Sun balance the orbital motion of a satellite, enabling continuous observation of the Sun.
 
• **Halo Orbit:** A stable orbit around L1 that allows spacecraft to maintain their position and observe celestial objects without interference.
 
• **Aditya-L1 Payloads:** The spacecraft carries seven scientific instruments, including the Visible Emission Line Coronagraph (VELC) and Solar Ultraviolet Imaging Telescope (SUIT).
 
• **Significance of Aditya-L1:** The mission aims to deepen our understanding of solar phenomena such as coronal mass ejections, solar flares, and their impact on space weather.
 
• **INSAT Series:** These satellites are primarily used for meteorological observations, telecommunications, and broadcasting services, and are unrelated to solar studies.

questions.question: In July 2025, the National Green Tribunal has imposed a total fine of Rs. 23.7 crore on authorities in __________ over green belt pollution.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttar Pradesh**__.
 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__
 __ 
• In **July 2025**, the **National Green Tribunal (NGT)** imposed a fine of **Rs. 23.7 crore** on authorities in **Uttar Pradesh** for **pollution in green belts**. 
• The NGT criticized the local authorities for their **failure to control pollution** and uphold environmental regulations within the green belt areas. 
• The fine was imposed under the provisions of the **Environment Protection Act, 1986**, which empowers authorities to penalize violations of environmental norms. 
• This action was part of the ongoing efforts by the NGT to address **environmental degradation** caused by industrial, vehicular, and other pollutants in urban and semi-urban areas. 
• The green belt areas, which are meant to act as **buffers against pollution**, have been adversely affected due to unregulated activities, leading to this strong punitive measure. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **National Green Tribunal (NGT):** 
• The NGT was established in **2010** under the **National Green Tribunal Act** to handle cases related to environmental protection and conservation of forests and other natural resources. 
• It has the power to impose penalties and provide compensation for environmental damages. 
• The tribunal ensures the effective and expeditious disposal of cases related to environmental issues. 
• **Green Belt Importance:** 
• Green belts are areas with **vegetation and trees** that help reduce urban heat, improve air quality, and act as noise barriers. 
• They play a significant role in **mitigating the effects of pollution** by absorbing carbon dioxide and producing oxygen. 
• These areas are critical for maintaining ecological balance in urban and semi-urban regions. 
• **Environment Protection Act, 1986:** 
• It is an umbrella legislation enacted for the protection and improvement of the environment. 
• The act empowers authorities to take measures to prevent pollution and penalize violators of environmental laws. 
• It also provides for the regulation of industries and activities that impact the environment. 
• **Pollution in Uttar Pradesh:** 
• Uttar Pradesh has been grappling with high levels of pollution, particularly in cities like **Kanpur, Lucknow, and Ghaziabad**, which often feature in the list of most polluted cities in India. 
• Industrial emissions, vehicular pollution, and improper waste management are significant contributors to environmental degradation in the state. 
• The fine imposed by the NGT is a wake-up call for authorities to take stringent measures to curb pollution. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Role of NGT in Environmental Protection:** 
• The NGT has been instrumental in enforcing environmental norms and holding authorities accountable for lapses. 
• It has passed several landmark orders related to air and water pollution, waste management, and conservation of biodiversity. 
• **Significance of Green Belts:** 
• Green belts act as **lungs of urban areas**, providing cleaner air and reducing the urban heat island effect. 
• They also serve as habitats for flora and fauna, contributing to biodiversity conservation. 
• **Pollution Control Measures:** 
• Strict enforcement of emission norms for industries and vehicles. 
• Promotion of renewable energy and sustainable practices to reduce dependence on fossil fuels. 
• Effective waste management practices, including segregation and recycling of waste. </ul

questions.question: The National Infrastructure Pipeline was launched in India in ___.

questions.question:
Consider the statements about Dumhal:

1. Exclusively Wattal men plant a banner before dancing.

2. It celebrates apple harvests in southern Kashmir.

Which is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1 correct**__.

__

• **Dumhal** is a traditional folk dance performed by the **Wattal tribe of Kashmir**.

• The dance is **exclusively performed by the men of the Wattal tribe**, who plant a ceremonial banner or flag into the ground before starting the dance. *Hence, statement 1 is correct.*

• The dance does not have any specific connection with the celebration of the **apple harvest in southern Kashmir**. It is a ritualistic dance performed on certain occasions and does not commemorate specific agricultural events. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*

• The performers wear colorful costumes and move in a circular motion around the planted flag while singing and dancing to rhythmic music.

• The Dumhal is regarded as one of the most unique and vibrant dance forms of Jammu and Kashmir, showcasing the rich cultural heritage of the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__

• **Wattal Tribe:**

• The Wattal tribe is a small community in Jammu and Kashmir known for its unique cultural traditions and practices.

• The tribe is primarily involved in performing arts and holds a significant place in Kashmiri folklore.

• **Costumes and Musical Instruments:**

• The performers of Dumhal wear long, flowing, and colorful robes, often adorned with beads and ornaments.

• Musical instruments such as drums and traditional Kashmiri flutes are used to accompany the dance.

• **Purpose of Dumhal:**

• Dumhal is performed on special occasions, including religious ceremonies and cultural celebrations.

• It is considered a sacred dance and is often associated with invoking blessings and honoring traditions.

• **Other Folk Dances of Jammu and Kashmir:**

• **Rouf:** A popular dance performed by Kashmiri women during festivals and celebrations.

• **Bacha Nagma:** Performed by young boys dressed as women, this dance is a significant part of Kashmiri weddings.

• **Hikat:** A traditional dance where performers hold hands and move in a circular motion.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Geographical Context:**

• Kashmir is known for its rich and diverse cultural heritage, with dance and music playing a crucial role in its traditions.

• The region’s unique topography and climate have influenced its cultural practices, including the attire and themes of folk dances.

• **Significance of Folk Dances:**

• Folk dances like Dumhal serve as a medium for storytelling and preserving the community's history and heritage.

• They also play a role in fostering social cohesion and identity within the tribal and rural communities of Kashmir.

• **Preservation Efforts:**

• Various cultural organizations and government initiatives are working to preserve traditional art forms like Dumhal.

• Efforts include organizing cultural festivals and providing platforms for tribal communities to showcase their heritage.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is incorrect regarding global indices as of July 2025?

options.text: The World Happiness Report 2024 highlights social support, life expectancy, and GDP per capita as key happiness factors.
AQI consistently above 200 signals general health risks and requires urgent policy action.
Despite being discontinued, the Ease of Doing Business report remains influential for investors assessing startup procedures.
A rise in GNI per capita alone can significantly improve HDI, even with falling life expectancy and education.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Human Development Index (HDI) is calculated using three primary indicators: life expectancy, education (mean years and expected years), and GNI per capita (Gross National Income).
 
• A rise in GNI per capita alone cannot significantly improve the HDI score if other parameters like life expectancy and education decline.
 
• The HDI approach emphasizes balanced improvement across all dimensions for holistic human development assessment.
 
• Global HDI rankings and trends reflect a country's socio-economic and public health development over time.
 
• The claim that "a rise in GNI per capita alone can significantly improve HDI, even with falling life expectancy and education" is incorrect, as HDI depends on simultaneous performance across all indicators.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Human Development Index (HDI):**

 
 
• Developed by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) to measure a country's overall achievement in its social and economic dimensions.
 
• HDI is a composite index based on three dimensions: health (life expectancy), education, and standard of living (GNI per capita).
 
• It is widely used to compare development levels among nations and regions.
 
 
 
• **Gross National Income (GNI):**
 
 
• GNI represents the total income earned by a country's residents and businesses, including income from abroad.
 
• It is an important economic indicator used in HDI calculation to reflect the standard of living.
 
 
 
• **Life Expectancy:**
 
 
• Life expectancy serves as a proxy for the health dimension in HDI.
 
• It reflects the average number of years a person is expected to live, based on current mortality rates.
 
 
 
• **Education Indicators in HDI:**
 
 
• Mean years of schooling (average years of education received by people aged 25 and older).
 
• Expected years of schooling (number of years a child of school-entry age is expected to spend in school).
 
 
 
• **Balanced Development:**
 
 
• Improvement in one dimension (e.g., GNI) cannot compensate for declines in others (e.g., education or health).
 
• Holistic growth across all dimensions is crucial for sustainable human development.

questions.question: Announced in the Union Budget 2025-26, what is the primary objective of the National Geospatial Mission?

options.text: To create and manage an integrated geospatial infrastructure for governance and development
To promote satellite launch services for private companies
To provide free GPS services to rural areas
To monitor climate change patterns through satellite data

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To create and manage an integrated geospatial infrastructure for governance and development**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **National Geospatial Mission** aims to establish an integrated geospatial infrastructure to support governance and development activities across India.
 
• It focuses on ensuring geospatial data availability, accessibility, and usability for various stakeholders, including the government, private sector, and academia.
 
• The mission is designed to align with the vision of **Digital India**, promoting the use of geospatial technologies for decision-making and planning.
 
• It emphasizes the creation of a unified geospatial ecosystem by utilizing advanced technologies like Geographic Information Systems (GIS), remote sensing, and satellite imagery.
 
• The mission also promotes innovation and entrepreneurship in the geospatial domain, fostering the growth of India’s geospatial industry.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: To promote satellite launch services for private companies**

 
 
• India has been actively promoting its satellite launch capabilities through organizations like **ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation)**.
 
• The **IN-SPACe (Indian National Space Promotion and Authorization Center)** was established to encourage private sector participation in space activities, including satellite launches.
 
• However, this is not the primary focus of the National Geospatial Mission, as its objective is related to geospatial data and infrastructure, not satellite launch services.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: To provide free GPS services to rural areas**
 
 
• GPS (Global Positioning System) services are already accessible to the public across India, including rural areas, through smartphones and other devices.
 
• While geospatial technologies can enhance rural development, providing free GPS services is not the specific aim of the National Geospatial Mission.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: To monitor climate change patterns through satellite data**
 
 
• Satellite data is indeed critical for monitoring climate change patterns, and India has several missions like **INSAT, RISAT, and Cartosat** dedicated to such objectives.
 
• However, the National Geospatial Mission focuses broadly on geospatial infrastructure for governance and development, not exclusively on climate change monitoring.

questions.question: Sanjiv Ranjan assumed the role of secretary general of the which of the following organisation on January 1,2025?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__
 
• **Sanjiv Ranjan**, a seasoned diplomat, assumed the role of **Secretary General of the Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA)** on **January 1, 2025**. 
• The **Indian Ocean Rim Association (IORA)** is an intergovernmental organization that promotes regional cooperation and sustainable development within the Indian Ocean region. 
• The IORA was established in **1997** and comprises **23 member states** that share a coastline along the Indian Ocean, including countries such as India, Australia, South Africa, and Indonesia.

questions.question: The traditional folk festival 'Phuldei', marked by floral offerings and cultural rituals, is primarily observed in which Indian state?

• **Phuldei** is a traditional **folk festival** celebrated in the Indian state of **Uttarakhand**, primarily observed during the month of **March** to mark the arrival of spring. 
• It is a festival where young children visit houses in their villages and offer **flowers**, grains, and rice to the house's threshold, wishing prosperity and happiness for the inhabitants. 
• The festival is deeply rooted in the **cultural and religious traditions** of Uttarakhand and reflects the close bond between the people and nature. 
• Phuldei is celebrated with various **rituals and songs**. Children sing folk songs while offering floral tributes, and families prepare traditional dishes such as **‘Puri’ and ‘Singal’**. 
• This festival symbolizes **community harmony, gratitude, and the celebration of nature**, which are integral to the culture of Uttarakhand.

• **Uttarakhand:** 
• Uttarakhand, also known as the **"Devbhoomi" (Land of Gods)**, is a northern state in India, famous for its **natural beauty, religious heritage, and vibrant folk traditions**. 
• The state is rich in **flora and fauna**, and its traditions often revolve around the celebration of nature. 
• Other notable festivals celebrated in Uttarakhand include **Harela, Bikhauti, and Khatarua**. 
• Uttarakhand is divided into two regions: **Kumaon** and **Garhwal**, each having its own unique cultural practices and festivals. 
• The state offers picturesque landscapes, such as the **Himalayas, rivers (like Ganga and Yamuna), and forests**, making it a significant tourist destination. 
• **Other Indian States:**

• **Assam:** Celebrates festivals like **Bihu, Ambubachi Mela**, and **Durga Puja**, reflecting its rich tradition and agricultural significance. 
• **Punjab:** Known for its energetic festivals like **Lohri, Baisakhi**, and **Gurpurab**, showcasing the vibrancy of Punjabi culture. 
• **Important Points:** 
• Festivals like Phuldei highlight the **importance of preserving cultural heritage** and **environmental conservation**. 
• They provide a unique opportunity for communities to come together and celebrate their traditions, fostering **social unity**. 
• Traditional festivals often incorporate **seasonal changes**, agricultural practices, and gratitude towards nature, making them both culturally and ecologically significant.

• **'Show Business'** is a novel written by **Shashi Tharoor**, an Indian politician, diplomat, and author.

• The novel was first published in **1992**, and it remains one of Tharoor's most celebrated works in the field of fiction.

• He served as the **Under-Secretary-General of the United Nations** and has been a Member of Parliament for Thiruvananthapuram since 2009.
 
• Some of his other notable works include **'The Great Indian Novel'**, **'Inglorious Empire'**, and **'Why I Am a Hindu'**.
 
 
 
• **Bollywood Satire in 'Show Business':**
 
 
• The novel provides a critique of the **superficiality and commercialism** of Bollywood cinema.
 
• It portrays the struggles of an actor caught between personal values and professional demands.
 
• The book uses parody and exaggeration to shed light on the societal impact of cinema in India.

• Bollywood, the Indian film industry, is the largest in the world in terms of the number of films produced annually.
 
• It plays a crucial role in shaping cultural narratives and influencing public opinion in India.
 
• The industry has often been criticized for its formulaic approach, which 'Show Business' effectively satirizes.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• It provides an insider's view of Bollywood, highlighting the ethical dilemmas faced by actors and filmmakers.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Satire in Literature:**

questions.question: In May 2025, the Supreme Court set aside which High Court order that had denied maternity leave to a government school teacher for the birth of their third child?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__
 __ 
• In **May 2025**, the **Supreme Court of India** set aside an order passed by the **Madras High Court** that had denied maternity leave to a government school teacher for the birth of her third child. 
• The teacher had previously been denied maternity leave citing the **two-child policy**, which is a guideline followed in some government sectors to limit benefits to employees with only two children. 
• The Supreme Court ruled in favor of the teacher, emphasizing the importance of **maternity rights** and the welfare of children irrespective of birth order. 
• The judgment reaffirmed the principles of **gender equality** and **women's rights** guaranteed under the **Indian Constitution**, including **Article 42**, which directs the state to make provisions for securing just and humane conditions of work and maternity relief. 
• This decision has significant implications for **maternity leave policies** and reinforces the need to balance population control policies with the fundamental rights of individuals. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
 __ 
• **Madras High Court:** 
• The **Madras High Court** is one of the oldest High Courts in India, established in **1862**, and it has jurisdiction over the state of Tamil Nadu and the Union Territory of Puducherry. 
• It has been involved in several landmark cases, shaping the interpretation of laws and constitutional provisions in India. 
• **Maternity Benefits in India:** 
• The **Maternity Benefit Act, 1961**, as amended in **2017**, provides women with **26 weeks** of paid maternity leave for the first two children and **12 weeks** for subsequent children. 
• It applies to all establishments employing **10 or more workers**, aiming to ensure the health and well-being of both the mother and child. 
• **Supreme Court's Role in Protecting Women's Rights:** 
• The **Supreme Court of India** has consistently upheld women's rights, including maternity leave, as part of the fundamental rights under **Articles 14, 15, and 21** of the Constitution. 
• In past rulings, the Court has highlighted the need for a supportive work environment for women to balance their professional and personal responsibilities. 
• **Two-Child Policy:** 
• Some government policies in India, particularly in the past, have implemented a **two-child norm** to control population growth. 
• This norm has been criticized for being discriminatory and violating fundamental rights, especially when linked to eligibility for government benefits or employment. 
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**
 
• **Significance of Maternity Leave:** 
• Maternity leave is essential to ensure the health and well-being of the mother and child during and after pregnancy. 
• It also promotes **gender equality** in the workplace and encourages women’s participation in the workforce. 
• **Role of Judiciary:** 
• The judiciary plays a crucial role in interpreting and enforcing laws to protect women's rights, including maternity benefits. 
• Judgments such as this one set precedents that influence policies and promote social justice.

questions.question: Which country hosted the FIFA World Cup 2022?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Qatar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **FIFA World Cup 2022** was hosted by **Qatar**, making it the first time the tournament was held in the **Middle East region.**
 
• The tournament took place from **20 November to 18 December 2022**, coinciding with Qatar's National Day on the final match day.
 
• It was a unique edition as it was the **first FIFA World Cup to be held during the winter months** (November-December) due to the extreme summer heat in Qatar.
 
• Qatar invested heavily in infrastructure, spending approximately **$220 billion** to prepare for the tournament, including building **eight state-of-the-art stadiums**, transportation systems, and accommodations.
 
• **Argentina**, led by captain **Lionel Messi**, emerged as the champion after defeating **France** in the final, which ended in a dramatic penalty shootout (3-3 in regular time, 4-2 in penalties).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Key Features of Qatar’s FIFA World Cup:**

 
 
• The tournament featured **32 teams** from across the globe, competing in **64 matches**.
 
• Qatar constructed **8 new stadiums**, including the famous **Lusail Iconic Stadium**, which hosted the final match.
 
• Sustainability was a priority, with the **Stadium 974** being the first fully demountable stadium in World Cup history, made from shipping containers.
 
• Qatar showcased its rich culture and traditions, blending football with its heritage to offer a unique experience for fans worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Notable Moments:**
 
 
• The 2022 edition saw several upsets, including **Saudi Arabia’s historic win against Argentina** in the group stage.
 
• Morocco became the first African team to reach the **semi-finals**, creating history and inspiring the continent.
 
• **Lionel Messi** won the **Golden Ball** for being the best player of the tournament, while **Kylian Mbappé** was awarded the **Golden Boot** for scoring the most goals (8).
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact:**
 
 
• Hosting the FIFA World Cup boosted Qatar’s global image and economy, attracting tourists and investments.
 
• The tournament led to significant growth in the hospitality and transportation sectors, with millions of visitors attending the event.
 
 
 
• **Other Host Countries in FIFA History:**
 
 
• **Russia** hosted the FIFA World Cup in **2018**, where France won the championship.
 
• **Brazil** hosted in **2014**, with Germany emerging as the winner.
 
• Future hosts include **Canada, Mexico, and the USA** in **2026**, marking the first tri-nation World Cup.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Why Qatar’s Selection Was Historic:**

 
 
• Qatar was chosen to host the tournament in **2010** by the FIFA Executive Committee.
 
• This marked the first time the FIFA World Cup was held in the **Arab world**, promoting inclusivity and regional representation in football.
 
• The decision faced scrutiny and criticism over **human rights concerns** and working conditions for migrant laborers. However, Qatar implemented reforms to address these issues.
 
 
 
• **Technological Innovations:**
 
 
• The 2022 World Cup introduced the **semi-automated offside technology** for more accurate and faster referee decisions.
 
• State-of-the-art cooling systems were used in stadiums to ensure comfortable conditions for players and fans.

questions.question: What is the primary objective of the **'e-SafeHER'** initiative launched by **Reliance Foundation** and **C-DAC**?

options.text: To provide vocational training in hardware repair for urban youth
To establish a national network of digital libraries in primary schools
To provide cybersecurity awareness training to one million women in rural India
To offer interest-free loans to women-led technology startups in metro cities

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To provide cybersecurity awareness training to one million women in rural India**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

• The core objective of **e-SafeHER** is to enable **one million women** across **rural India** to participate safely and confidently in the **digital ecosystem**.
 
• The initiative aims to strengthen **last-mile cybersecurity awareness**, specifically targeting women who are increasingly using digital platforms for **financial transactions**, livelihoods, and essential services.
 
• The program is anchored under **MeitY's Information Security Education and Awareness (ISEA)** programme, with **C-DAC Hyderabad** providing the curriculum and training material.
 
• **Reliance Foundation** will use its grassroots presence and **women's Self-Help Groups (SHGs)** to deliver this training through a community-based model.
 
• Through this initiative, the goal is to create **one million 'Cyber Sakhis'** in rural areas over the next **three years**, scaling up to the full target by **2029**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The programme will follow a phased approach, initially starting with the training of **Cyber Sakhis** across **Madhya Pradesh** and **Odisha**.
 
• **C-DAC** is responsible for the development, **localization**, and **multilingual adaptation** of the cybersecurity training content to ensure it is accessible to rural populations.
 
• The initiative is designed to be sustainable by embedding cybersecurity awareness into existing **digital literacy** and **women's empowerment** programmes without needing parallel infrastructure.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• The collaboration combines the **technical expertise** of **C-DAC** and **MeitY’s national framework** with the **grassroots reach** of **Reliance Foundation**.
 
• Expected outcomes include improved **cyber risk awareness**, increased confidence in **digital transactions**, and the adoption of **safe digital practices** by rural women.

questions.question: In which state is the newly designated 99th Ramsar site of India, the Shekha Jheel Bird Sanctuary, located?
questions.solution:

• Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change **Bhupender Yadav** announced the designation of **Shekha Jheel Bird Sanctuary** in **Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh**, as a **Ramsar site**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

• **Shekha Jheel Bird Sanctuary** is officially located in the district of **Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• This new designation makes it **Uttar Pradesh's 12th Ramsar site** and **India's 99th** overall, pushing the country closer to a milestone of 100 Ramsar sites.
 
• The recognition aims to support **local livelihoods, biodiversity conservation**, and ensure **water and climate security**.
 
• The sanctuary acts as a crucial stopover on the **Central Asian Flyway**, providing a vital winter habitat for migratory birds such as the **Bar-headed Goose, Painted Stork**, and various species of ducks.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• The continuous ecosystem restoration mission, highlighting India's commitment to wetland conservation, is being led by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] Important Points__**

 
• **Location of Shekha Jheel:** Aligarh, Uttar Pradesh.
